findingDetails.title: Corpus indexing accepts Markdown symlinks whose real target is outside the repository
findingDetails.evidence: The corpus walker records symlinked Markdown files by repo-relative link path without checking the resolved target is inside repoRoot, and generation reads through that link, allowing external file bytes to enter the committed index.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reject or explicitly report symlinked Markdown targets outside repoRoot, preferably fail-closed for generation, and add an out-of-tree symlink fixture.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Traced symlink walk, realpath deduplication, generator read path and existing in-tree symlink fixture; no target writes.

adjudication.claim: A Markdown symlink under a retrieval corpus root can cause an external file to be hashed and indexed as an internal-looking path.
adjudication.counterevidenceSought: Compared symlinked-directory pruning, in-repository file-link deduplication and generator path handling; searched for a canonical-target containment check.
adjudication.alternativeExplanation: Symlinked files may be trusted repository aliases; rejected because the implementation explicitly treats symlinked directories as a boundary and does not document external-file trust, while the generator publishes committed artifacts.
adjudication.downgradeTrigger: Constrain corpus roots to trusted real paths or document external symlink trust with a fixture and explicit provenance field.
